To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HIF-1 activation in MCF7 cells grown as 3-D aggregates induces the expression of the drug resistance protein P-glycoprotien and that this may be a mechanism for the resistance of IMPC to chemotherapy.

MCF7 cells grown as 3-D tumor spheroids, a morphological model of IMPC, are resistant to dox, an effect that is mediated by the activation of HIF1, which in turn increases the Pgp expression on cell surface.
MCF7 2D and 3D cultures differ in their sensitivity to doxorubicinin vitro, and that this difference can be ascribed to a different expression of Pgp, which is increased in 3D cultures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new model of chemo-resistance in breast cancer.
the development of new strategies to overcome the resistance of this aggressive breast cancer.
the identification of new therapeutic strategies for the treatment of breast cancer, in particular for the treatment of IMPC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIF-1 activation in MCF7 spheroids induces doxorubicine resistance by increasing the expression of P-glycoptein, a drug transporter.
MCF7 2-D monolayers and MCF7 4-D 3-D sphenoids are not equivalent in their response to HIF-1 inhibition and that the latter is a more suitable model to study HIF-1 activation in IMPC.
the 3-D spheric model of MCF7 cells may be used as a model of IMPC drug resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the activation of HIF pathway in MCF7 cells, when grown as 3D spheroids, is responsible for the induction of drug resistance via the upregulation of the expression of P-glyco-protein, a drug efflux pump.
the 3-D culture of breast cancer cells may represent a good model for studying the molecular mechanisms of drug resistance in IMPC.
the 3D model of MCF7 breast cancer spheroids can be used to study the mechanism of chemo-resistance in breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

HIF-1 activation is a mechanism for Pgp-mediated drug resistance in breast cancer cells and that the 3-D MCF7 spheroids model may be a useful tool to study the molecular basis of IMPC drug resistance and for the screening of new drugs.
HIF-1 activation may be a novel therapeutic target for IMPC.
HIF-1 activation is associated with P-glycoproteins expression in 3-D breast cancer cell spheroids, and that this may be a potential model of drug resistance of IMPC.
